statistics.cold: one PostgreSQL-buffer-cold measurement per independent outer or inner restart track; no OS, page-cache or device-cold claim
statistics.warm: median and maximum of seven measured runs after two unmeasured warm-ups in that same track
statistics.planning: maximum planning time across the cold run and seven measured warm runs, independently per track
statistics.suite: both independently reconstructed fresh-database suites must pass every mandatory case

generation.algorithm: counter-derived deterministic generation; no random API and no schema default is relied upon except generated columns and migration-owned role/permission seed rows
generation.uuidRule: RFC 4122 UUIDv5 using uuidNamespace and UTF-8 name input shown by each formula; lowercase canonical 8-4-4-4-12 text
generation.timestampRule: 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z plus the table-local zero-based row ordinal in seconds

authUsers.fillerNameInput: `${seed}:auth-fill:${userOrdinal3}` where userOrdinal3 is the zero-based user ordinal padded to exactly three decimal digits
authUsers.surface: temporary auth.users(id uuid primary key, email text not null unique)
authUsers.collisionRule: enumerate all 700 names, require 700 unique names, 700 unique UUIDv5 results and no actor/filler intersection before insert

restaurantUsers.authPairing: restaurant_users row at userOrdinal u has auth_user_id equal to auth.users.id at the same userOrdinal u
restaurantUsers.collisionRule: require 700 unique restaurant-user name inputs, 700 unique IDs, 700 unique auth_user_id values and every auth_user_id present in auth.users

identityMapping.nonOverrideMembershipUserRule: For each membershipSerial not in membershipUserOverrides, compute nonOverrideRank as its zero-based position in the ascending list of all non-override membershipSerial values, then userOrdinal=9+nonOverrideRank. The 671 ranks 0-670 map bijectively to user ordinals 9-679.
identityMapping.duplicateException: Only A05/userOrdinal 4 is assigned to multiple memberships: exactly tenant ordinals 1-10 at membership ordinal 0, producing 10 assignments and 9 duplicate assignments beyond its first. Every other membership user has exactly one membership.
identityMapping.membershipUserOrdinals: exact set {0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8} union integer range 9-679; 8 actor users + 671 filler users = 679
identityMapping.nonMemberDerivation: 700 total user ordinals minus 679 membership-user ordinals = 21; exact complement is actor A06 ordinal 5 plus filler ordinals 680-699

semanticHash.timing: after all 13 table datasets are materialized and before ANALYZE
semanticHash.algorithm: SHA-256 over the exact canonical envelope; output exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
semanticHash.envelope: A JSON array of 13 table objects. Each object has members table, columns and rows; RFC 8785 canonical serialization determines object-member order and string escaping. columns is the exact includedColumns array and each row is a JSON array in that column order.

rowOrder.auth.users: id ASC by lowercase UUID UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.restaurants: id ASC by text UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.restaurant_branches: id ASC by text UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.menus: id ASC by text UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.menu_categories: id ASC by text UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.menu_items: id ASC by text UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.branch_menu_items: id ASC by text UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.menu_item_nutrition: id ASC by text UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.restaurant_users: id ASC by lowercase UUID UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.restaurant_roles: id ASC by lowercase UUID UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.role_permissions: role_id, permission_key, permission_scope ASC by lowercase UUID then text UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.restaurant_memberships: id ASC by lowercase UUID UTF-8 bytes
rowOrder.restaurant_membership_branch_scopes: id ASC by lowercase UUID UTF-8 bytes

semanticHash.scalarCanonicalization: UUIDs are lowercase canonical 8-4-4-4-12 JSON strings; timestamps are UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ JSON strings; SQL text is a JSON string with no Unicode normalization; text arrays retain declared element order; null is JSON null; booleans are JSON true/false; SQL integer is a base-10 JSON integer with zero represented as 0 and no leading zeros; SQL numeric is a JSON string in non-exponent decimal form with no leading plus, no unnecessary leading zeros and no trailing fractional zeros, with zero represented as `0`.
semanticHash.bytes: RFC 8785 canonical JSON encoded as UTF-8, with no BOM, no insignificant whitespace, no separators outside JSON syntax and no trailing LF or other byte
semanticHash.seedRows: restaurant_roles and role_permissions are separate table objects in tableOrder; read their exact non-timestamp columns from the frozen migration seed, sort by their declared rowOrder, and exclude migration-time created_at defaults as shown by includedColumns
semanticHash.suiteRule: both independently reconstructed fresh suites must produce byte-identical canonical envelopes and identical hashes

cases.purpose: all max categories reachable through assigned branches

suiteOrder: run cases C01-P06 in caseId order with independent required tracks

analyze.timing: after semantic hash and before any workload case in both suites
commands: ANALYZE public.restaurants, public.restaurant_branches, public.menus, public.menu_categories, public.menu_items, public.branch_menu_items, public.menu_item_nutrition
analyze.failure: any ANALYZE error fails the suite

relationSize.primarySource: after ANALYZE, capture pg_class.reltuples by joining pg_class.relnamespace=pg_namespace.oid; require nspname plus relname and save relid OID, schema-qualified identity and reltuples for every generated base table
relationSize.generatedCountCrossCheck: round reltuples to nearest integer; it must equal the exact generated count for these non-sampled table sizes or the suite fails; never choose the more favorable source
relationSize.rounding: PostgreSQL reltuples float is rounded half away from zero only for the equality cross-check; scan fractions use the unrounded positive reltuples
relationSize.missingOrNegative: missing, null or negative reltuples fails before workload

planRelationResolution.baseNode: only a plan node with Schema and Relation Name is a base-relation scan; resolve exact nspname/relname to the captured OID, while Alias is evidence only
planRelationResolution.derivedNodes: CTE Scan, Subquery Scan, Function Scan, Values Scan and nodes without Schema/Relation Name receive no relation-size rule
planRelationResolution.partition: each child base relation is evaluated by its own OID; Append/Gather parents are not counted as scans
planRelationResolution.parallel: use leader-aggregated node Actual Rows and Actual Loops once; do not add per-worker detail arrays a second time

sequentialScanAlgorithm.collection: walk the complete inner JSON plan tree; group every base-relation node with Node Type exactly Seq Scan by resolved OID
sequentialScanAlgorithm.effectiveExecutions: sum Actual Loops across all grouped Seq Scan nodes; missing/non-finite/negative Actual Loops fails
sequentialScanAlgorithm.largeRepeated: if unrounded analyzed reltuples >512 and effectiveExecutions >1, fail
sequentialScanAlgorithm.largeSingle: if reltuples >512 and effectiveExecutions exactly 1, the sole node passes only when returnedFraction>=0.25, rowsRemoved<=2*returnedRows and that node Shared Hit Blocks/Shared Read Blocks are each within the case inner limits
sequentialScanAlgorithm.returnedRows: Actual Rows * Actual Loops for the sole node
sequentialScanAlgorithm.rowsRemoved: (Rows Removed by Filter + Rows Removed by Join Filter, missing fields treated as zero) * Actual Loops
sequentialScanAlgorithm.returnedFraction: returnedRows / unrounded reltuples; no rounding before comparison
sequentialScanAlgorithm.zeroReturn: zero returned rows on a large single Seq Scan fails the 25% rule
sequentialScanAlgorithm.small: reltuples <=512 permits Seq Scan, still subject to all case-wide buffer, spill, estimation, fan-out and nested-loop limits

outerTrack: poll the exact test port until connection refusal; timeout fails
new session with jit=off, track_io_timing=on and statement_timeout=15000ms
one measured PostgreSQL-buffer-cold exact RPC EXPLAIN plan
two unmeasured exact outer RPC warm-ups
seven measured exact outer RPC EXPLAIN plans
evaluate outer cold execution/read, warm median, warm maximum and planning maximum; preserve outer metrics separately
innerTrack: poll exact port closed again; timeout fails
one measured PostgreSQL-buffer-cold verified body-derived inner EXPLAIN plan
evaluate inner cold execution/read, warm median, warm maximum, planning maximum and plan rules; preserve inner metrics separately
execution.coldBoundary: Outer and inner cold evidence always comes from different restart cycles for every applicable case in both suites. This is PostgreSQL-buffer-cold only; OS/page-cache/device cold is not claimed.
execution.payload: For required outer evidence, invoke the exact RPC under the synthetic actor and compute canonical payload bytes as octet_length(convert_to(COALESCE(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(r) ORDER BY the function identityKey),'[]'::jsonb)::text,'UTF8')); PostgreSQL 17.6 jsonb text is the authority serialization. Ordering is measurement-only and does not claim the RPC is ordered. Count comes from the same rows.
execution.bodyExtraction: Normalize the migration to LF; lex CREATE FUNCTION through AS followed by its exact dollar delimiter; capture until the matching delimiter token followed by semicolon. The outer delimiter is not part of the body. Tagged dollar quotes inside a differently delimited body are lexer content and cannot terminate extraction. Require one exact signature and hash extracted UTF-8 bytes before transformation.

states: quoted identifier with doubled double-quote escape
standard single-quoted string with doubled quote escape
E-prefixed escaped string with backslash and doubled-quote handling
lexer.identifierRule: In normal code, PostgreSQL unquoted identifier start [A-Za-z_ or non-ASCII] and continuation [A-Za-z0-9_$ or non-ASCII]; fold ASCII to lower case for comparison. Quoted identifiers never match.
lexer.replacement: After body hash verification, tokenize once and count only complete unquoted identifier tokens equal after folding to p_restaurant_id. Require parameterTokens, replace only those token spans with $1, tokenize again and require zero remaining matching identifiers. Strings, quoted identifiers, comments at any nesting depth and dollar-quoted content are immutable.
lexer.binding: PREPARE a unique per-case statement with exactly one text parameter for parameterized bodies and bind arguments.p_restaurant_id through EXECUTE; zero-input functions use the untouched extracted body and no PREPARE parameter.

execution.innerPlanEvidence: Walk non-opaque body-derived JSON plans and capture node type, schema/relation/alias, index name, join type, actual/planned rows, loops, rows removed, shared/local/temp buffers, sort method/space/type, hash batches/memory and settings.
execution.authorizationEvidence: Only exact outer function calls under transaction-local request.jwt.claim.sub prove authorization and row disposition. Inner plans never substitute for outer authorization evidence.
execution.diagnosticDisposition: P01-P06 are diagnostic inner-only cases. Failure is recorded and does not fail the mandatory suite, but P2V-PERF-001 cannot be closed while a diagnostic failure lacks an explicit reviewed disposition.
execution.mandatoryDisposition: Any missing required track or any authorization, row, payload, threshold, body, schema, security, relation-size or determinism failure in C01-N03 or D01-D10 fails that suite; both fresh suites must pass.
execution.artifacts: All runner, generated rows, plans, logs, database and PostgreSQL files live in one repository-external temporary directory and are removed after sanitized reporting.
